claims.statement: Polish tariff rules provide specific charges for exceeding contracted active power, calculated from recorded power excesses, and provide correction procedures for billing or metering errors.
TAURON publicly explains that excessive reactive-energy consumption is charged separately by delivery point and that customers must remain within both reactive-power and contracted-power limits.

Hypothesis: a portfolio-level scanner sold on verified savings can reach sites ignored by traditional energy audits, but the frequency and magnitude of avoidable charges must be established from real invoices.

contrary_evidence: Electrical contractors and energy consultants already diagnose reactive power and can bundle hardware with an audit.
Many SMEs have charges too small or too volatile to support a meaningful success fee.

economics.acquisition_route: Scan invoices from family-business customers, then let electrical contractors offer the no-upfront audit during service visits
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1,000 monitored sites at about 3.6k PLN ARR plus 1M PLN annual success fees produce 4.6M PLN revenue and 1.8M PLN EBITDA by year 5. At 4x EBITDA and 70% ownership, equity reaches about 5M PLN in years 5 to 7.
economics.founder_time: 10 to 16 hours weekly for model QA and partner enablement after the first twenty audited portfolios
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 70% to 85% for software audits; inspection and installation are pass-through partner services
economics.payback: Pricing is funded from measured savings; the customer keeps at least 80% in year 1 and nearly all recurring savings thereafter
economics.pricing: 20% of verified first-year savings plus 199 to 399 PLN per site monthly monitoring
economics.retention_or_repeat: New invoices, load changes, equipment additions, tariff revisions, and additional sites create recurring value

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A delivery-point ledger connecting invoice patterns, interval load, implemented remediation, equipment type, and realized savings
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs operating 20 to 200 electricity delivery points with motors, refrigeration, HVAC, or variable load
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Electrical contractors, renewable installers, bookkeeping platforms, franchise associations, and equipment lessors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Portfolio invoice scan, counterfactual tariff and power model, remediation brief, savings verification, and recurring alerts
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The operator pays a share of independently verified first-year savings and then a per-site monitoring fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A monthly invoice contains reactive-energy charges, contracted-power excesses, or an unexplained distribution-cost increase

founder_fit: Strong quantitative billing use case with a practical installer channel through the family company. The founder can automate invoice parsing and counterfactuals part-time, while qualified partners inspect and install; success-fee pricing reduces high-energy outbound selling.
risks: Poor baselines can overstate savings or recommend a harmful capacity change.
Installer commissions could compromise vendor neutrality and customer trust.
Hardware remediation requires qualified electricians and clear liability boundaries.

structure.critical_dependency: The target segments must have frequent, material, and technically remediable charges visible in accessible data

thesis: Launch a success-fee audit and verification layer for Polish multi-site grocers, bakeries, cold stores, gyms, and light manufacturers. It would ingest electricity invoices and interval data, isolate reactive-energy and contracted-capacity penalties by delivery point, simulate tariff and compensation changes, generate a vendor-neutral remediation brief, and verify savings after an electrician acts. The family renewable company provides an installer channel, while the product owns the invoice-to-action-to-savings ledger rather than selling capacitors.
title: Reactive-Power and Contract-Capacity Recovery for Multi-Site SMEs
uncertainties: Prevalence and median avoidable annual charge by the selected multi-site segments.
Availability and format of interval meter data across DSOs and tariff groups.
Whether clients will share invoices continuously after a one-time recovery.
